title: PostgreSQL is the only database for billing
decision: All billing data lives in PostgreSQL; no second datastore for invoices or payments.
rationale: Invoices and payments must change in one transaction. A document store was rejected for lacking that.

title: No caching of prices in checkout
decision: Checkout reads prices from the pricing service on every request.
rationale: A stale price shown to a customer is a legal problem. A 5-minute cache was tried and reverted.

title: Releases go out on Tuesdays
decision: Production releases happen once a week, on Tuesday morning.
rationale: Support needs predictable dates and nobody wants a Friday incident.

title: Feature flags for every user-facing change
decision: Any change a user can see ships behind a feature flag that defaults to off.
rationale: It lets us release on Tuesday and turn features on separately. Long-lived branches were ruled out.

title: TypeScript for all new frontend code
decision: New frontend modules are written in TypeScript with strict mode on.
rationale: Two production bugs last quarter were type errors. Gradual typing with JSDoc was considered too weak.

title: No new microservices without an owner team
decision: A new service needs a named owning team and an on-call rota before it is created.
rationale: Three orphaned services caused the March outage.

title: Mobile apps support the last two OS versions
decision: iOS and Android apps support the current and previous major OS version only.
rationale: Older versions are under 3 percent of sessions and block new platform APIs.

title: Passwords are never logged
decision: Request logging strips password, token and card fields before anything is written.
rationale: A log leak must not become a credential leak. Masking at the log viewer was rejected as too late.

title: Customer data stays in the EU region
decision: Customer records are stored and processed only in EU data centres.
rationale: Contracts with two enterprise customers require it, and so does GDPR for our use.

title: Third-party scripts need security review
decision: No third-party JavaScript is added to the web app without a security review.
rationale: A marketing tag once exfiltrated form fields. Self-hosting is preferred where possible.

title: REST for public API, no GraphQL
decision: The public API stays REST with versioned URLs.
rationale: Partners integrate with generic HTTP tools. GraphQL was evaluated and rejected for rate-limiting complexity.

title: Breaking API changes need 6 months notice
decision: A breaking change to the public API is announced at least six months before removal.
rationale: Partners release slowly; a shorter window broke two integrations.

title: All money amounts are integers in minor units
decision: Amounts are stored and passed as integer cents, never floating point.
rationale: Rounding errors in floats caused a reconciliation gap.

title: Search runs on OpenSearch
decision: Product search uses the managed OpenSearch cluster.
rationale: Postgres full-text was too slow past 2 million products. Algolia was rejected on cost.

title: Push notifications are opt-in
decision: The app asks before sending push notifications and sends none by default.
rationale: App store guidelines and a spike in uninstalls after the unsolicited campaign.

title: No personal data in analytics events
decision: Analytics events carry an anonymous id; names, emails and phone numbers are forbidden.
rationale: The analytics vendor is outside the EU.

title: Background jobs must be idempotent
decision: Every queue job can run twice without changing the result.
rationale: The queue delivers at least once. A duplicate refund job paid a customer twice.

title: Infrastructure is defined in Terraform
decision: Cloud resources are created through Terraform; console changes are reverted.
rationale: Manual changes made the staging and production environments drift apart.

title: Code review by one other engineer is mandatory
decision: Every pull request needs approval from one engineer who did not write it.
rationale: Required by our SOC 2 controls. Two approvals slowed delivery with no fewer defects.

title: Images are served through the CDN only
decision: Product images are uploaded to object storage and served via the CDN, never from app servers.
rationale: App servers ran out of disk during the holiday sale.

title: Support tickets are answered within one business day
decision: First response to any support ticket is due within one business day.
rationale: Agreed with sales as part of the standard contract.

title: No dark patterns in cancellation
decision: A subscription can be cancelled in two clicks from account settings.
rationale: Regulators fined a competitor, and retention offers before cancel were ruled out by legal.

title: Email is sent through one provider
decision: Transactional and marketing email both go through the same provider account.
rationale: Two providers gave us two suppression lists and we emailed unsubscribed users.

title: Accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA for new screens
decision: New screens must pass WCAG 2.1 AA before release.
rationale: Public sector customers require it in procurement.

title: Secrets live in the vault, not in env files
decision: Credentials are read from the secrets vault at start-up; .env files are for local development only.
rationale: A committed .env file exposed a payment key.

title: Dates are stored in UTC
decision: All timestamps are stored in UTC and converted in the client.
rationale: Daylight-saving bugs in the booking calendar.

title: Refunds above 500 need manager approval
decision: A refund over 500 in account currency requires approval from a support manager.
rationale: Fraud review found refund abuse concentrated in large amounts.

title: No AI-generated replies sent to customers without review
decision: Drafts written by an AI assistant are reviewed by a support agent before sending.
rationale: An unreviewed reply promised a refund policy we do not have.

title: One design system for web and mobile
decision: Web and mobile use the shared design system components; one-off components need design sign-off.
rationale: Three button styles shipped in one quarter.

title: Load tests before every major launch
decision: A launch expected to double traffic needs a load test at three times the forecast.
rationale: The spring campaign took checkout down for forty minutes.
